question: Should OpenClaw provide a general outbound agent-attestation contract, and if so what signer authority, verifier-key distribution, privacy policy, and egress paths are part of its guarantee?
rationale: This determines whether the feature is an identity signal, a cryptographically verifiable security boundary, or should remain an integration-specific concern; code review cannot safely choose that trust model.

options.title: Design a scoped core contract
options.body: Define a domain-allowlisted attestation API with explicit signer and verifier ownership before authorizing implementation.

options.title: Keep attestation integration-owned
options.body: Document provider- or service-specific authentication patterns and avoid a general OpenClaw origin-attestation guarantee.

options.title: Defer pending permissions work
options.body: Revisit after the skill-permission and trust-manifest direction is settled so the two contracts do not conflict.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped core contract
recommendation.body: Define a domain-allowlisted attestation API with explicit signer and verifier ownership before authorizing implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing product/security review and recent human-review label indicate the strongest available routing connection.
